messages.author: 74a522eefdfed5da
messages.subject: tableOutput does not print the data.frame
parts:
Hi,
I'm having some trouble with a reactiveTable output that is not being output by tableOutput. 
The reactive function createTable() returns a data frame. I've checked that it returns the expected result. When I change the output$tbl function to a reactiveText (along with the ui.R file) and call xtable manually, it displays the table correctly. Any help would be marvelous, as I'm struggling to find the answer.

The server function in question:
output$tbl = reactiveTable(function() {
    
    xt = createTable()
    
    lbls = getLabels()
    lbls = rbind(lbls, "Freq", "Combination")
    colnames(xt) = lbls$DEPT_NAME
    return(xt)
  }, include.rownames=FALSE)

Adam

The easiest way to help you would be if you could post your app up on gist.github.com and send us the URL. However, if you can't do that, here are some pointers that may help with debugging:

1) You can insert a browser() call right before the return, and from the browse prompt look and see if xt is the value you expect.
2) You can set options(shiny.trace=TRUE) before launching the app, then you will see the traffic going back and forth from the browser and R being printed to your R console. If you can make sense of the JSON format then you should be able to see if anything sensible is being sent from R to the client.
3) Do you see any errors/warnings being printed either at the R console, or the JavaScript error console in your browser?

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: tableOutput does not print the data.frame
parts:
Waaaaait a minute. Here's the source code for reactiveTable:

function (func, ...) 
{
    reactive(function() {
        classNames <- getOption("shiny.table.class", "data table table-bordered table-condensed")
        data <- func()
        if (is.null(data) || is.na(data)) 
            return("")
        return(paste(capture.output(print(xtable(data, ...), 
            type = "html", html.table.attributes = paste("class=\"", 
                htmlEscape(classNames, TRUE), "\"", sep = ""), 
            ...)), collapse = "\n"))
    })
}

The problem is in bold. is.na works "element-wise" so it returns a dataframe filled with TRUE/FALSE; when this is then OR'd with is.null(data) it is silently converted to TRUE.

This is a bug, we will need to fix it in 0.2.5. Thanks!!
